passage:
In the school courtyard in Lisbon, Tiago caught up with Beatriz after maths. "Who were you with at lunch?"
"Lindiwe and the girls from chemistry. Why?"
"Just asking." Then, later, on the tram home: "Can I see your chats? Just so I know. I only want the truth, Bia. Because I care."
She hesitated, then handed him her phone. He scrolled through her messages with Lindiwe, frowned at a joke about a boy in their class, and asked who "R" was. It was her grandmother, Rosa.
That evening Beatriz deleted a harmless voice note from Lindiwe before Tiago could see it, then felt strange for doing it. She hadn't done anything wrong. So why was she hiding things?
She looked out at the river. It had started to feel less like being loved and more like being watched.

qa.q: Who was 'R' in Beatriz's chats?
qa.a: 'R' was her grandmother, Rosa.

qa.q: Why did Beatriz feel strange after deleting the voice note?
qa.a: Beatriz hadn't done anything wrong, yet Tiago's checking had made her start hiding innocent things.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Beatriz here?
qa.a: Beatriz could tell Tiago clearly that checking her phone makes her feel watched, and talk to a trusted adult or counsellor if it continues.

qa.q: How does Tiago see his own checking?
qa.a: Tiago believes he only wants the truth because he cares, and doesn't see that it feels like being watched to Beatriz.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy questioning his girlfriend and asking to see her chats in the name of truth, while she feels watched and starts hiding small things.

passage:
The coaching centre corridor was crowded at break, and Irfan had been waiting by the water cooler for Pooja since the bell.
"Who were you talking to in the chemistry batch?" he asked before she'd even reached him.
"Rohit. He asked about the test."
"For ten minutes?"
"Irfan, it wasn't ten minutes."
"Show me the group chat, then. If there's nothing, what's the problem?"
Pooja glanced at the students passing, then held out her phone. He read it standing right there, thumb flicking fast. Nothing. He handed it back. "See? I just needed to know. It's because I care about you."
Pooja nodded, but in the next class she put her phone deep in her bag and switched off message previews. She told herself it was for concentration. It wasn't.

qa.q: Where was Irfan waiting for Pooja?
qa.a: Irfan was waiting by the water cooler.

qa.q: Why did Pooja switch off her message previews?
qa.a: Pooja felt watched and wanted to keep small, innocent things private from Irfan, even while telling herself it was for concentration.

qa.q: What could Irfan notice about his own behaviour?
qa.a: Irfan could notice that demanding to see chats comes from fear, not care, and that it is making Pooja hide things; talking to a counsellor could help him.

qa.q: How did being checked in the corridor feel for Pooja?
qa.a: Pooja likely felt embarrassed and pressured, glancing at the passing students before handing over her phone.

grounding: Illustrates a teen boy demanding to see his girlfriend's chats and calling it care, while she feels watched and begins to hide things.

passage:
In the boys' hostel common room at the residential school in Dehradun, Sachin waited by the phone booth until Ruhi came to the Sunday call.

"Who were you with at the library yesterday?" he asked, before hello.

"Just the study group. Asif, Mahi, Kavin."

"Asif again?"

"He's in the group, Sachin."

"Show me your chats with him when we meet. I just want to know the truth. That's all."

There was a pause. "Why would I need to show you my chats?"

"If there's nothing, what's the problem?"

Ruhi's voice went small. "Okay. Fine."

On Monday she deleted a harmless joke Asif had sent about the chemistry teacher. Not because it was anything. Because she could already hear Sachin's questions.

Sachin, on his end, told himself it was because he cared so much.

qa.q: Who was in Ruhi's study group, according to her?
qa.a: Asif, Mahi and Kavin.

qa.q: What does Sachin tell himself about why he asks these questions?
qa.a: He tells himself he just wants the truth and that it is because he cares so much, though underneath he seems insecure and afraid.

qa.q: What went wrong in how Sachin handled his worry?
qa.a: He demanded to see her chats instead of talking about his own fear, which made Ruhi feel watched; he could admit feeling insecure instead.

qa.q: How does Ruhi experience Sachin's questions?
qa.a: She feels watched and pressured, not loved, and begins deleting harmless messages to avoid more questions.

grounding: Sachin asks who Ruhi was with and demands to see her chats, calling it wanting the truth, while she feels watched and starts hiding small things.

passage:
Maria,

I'm writing because every time we talk it turns into a fight.

I don't understand why you won't just show me your phone. I've shown you mine. When you were at Carl's party on Saturday, I asked who was there and you said "people." That's not an answer. I just want to know the truth. Is that so much?

You said last week that I make you feel like you're being watched. That hurt. I'm not watching you. I'm just asking questions any boyfriend would ask.

Then yesterday I saw you close a chat window the second I walked over. What was that? If there's nothing, why hide it?

I love you. That's why I care so much. I just need you to be honest with me.

Baljeet

qa.q: Whose party was Maria at on Saturday?
qa.a: Carl's party.

qa.q: What is Baljeet feeling while writing this letter?
qa.a: Baljeet feels hurt, anxious and suspicious, convinced the questions come from love and a wish for the truth.

qa.q: What would you advise Baljeet after rereading this letter?
qa.a: To notice that demanding Maria's phone is making Maria hide things, and to talk honestly about the insecurity underneath, perhaps with a counsellor or trusted adult.

qa.q: How does Maria experience Baljeet's questions, based on what Maria said last week?
qa.a: Maria feels watched, and has started closing chats when Baljeet comes near, hiding small things to avoid more questions.

grounding: Baljeet's letter shows Baljeet demanding to see Maria's chats and calling it love and truth, while Maria feels watched and starts hiding small things.

passage:
I'm Tashi. You asked how things went wrong with Dolma, so I'll tell you straight. I thought I was being a good boyfriend. I really did.

Every time she went out with Rehana and the others, I texted. "Who's there?" "Which boys?" "Send a photo." When she came back I'd ask to see her phone. Just to be sure. I told her, "I only want the truth. If you love me, you'll show me."

She showed me, the first few times. Then she started leaving her phone at home. Then she stopped telling me when she went out. I found out from Rehana's story that she'd been at the momo place without me.

I was so angry. I thought, see, she's hiding things.

It took me a long time to understand. She wasn't hiding because of what she did. She was hiding because of what I did.

qa.q: Where did Tashi find out Dolma had been?
qa.a: At the momo place, from Rehana's story.

qa.q: How did Tashi feel when he found out from Rehana's story?
qa.a: He felt angry, taking it as proof that Dolma was hiding things.

qa.q: What did Tashi come to understand, and what could he have done differently?
qa.a: That his checking made Dolma hide things; he could have looked at his own insecurity instead of demanding her phone.

qa.q: How did Dolma experience Tashi's checking?
qa.a: She felt watched rather than loved, so she started leaving her phone at home and not telling him when she went out.

grounding: Tashi describes demanding Dolma's phone and calling it love and truth, and how she felt watched and began hiding small things.

Monday. Baljeet waited outside the computer lab. "Who were you sitting with?"
"Gauri and Salma."
"Just them?"
Himani nodded, puzzled. He smiled. He only wanted the truth, he told himself.
Wednesday. At the canteen he held out his hand. "Show me your chats. If there's nothing, what's the problem?" Himani gave a nervous laugh and passed him the phone. He scrolled for a long time. Her friends at the next table went quiet.
The following Monday. Himani stayed back after class to talk to her cousin, then told Baljeet she had been in the library. It was a tiny, pointless lie, and she felt sick telling it. That night he asked again who she had been with, and she heard herself answering carefully, like someone being watched. Baljeet called all of it caring. To Himani, it had started to feel like a cage.

qa.q: What did Baljeet ask to see at the canteen on Wednesday?
qa.a: He asked Himani to show him her chats.

qa.q: What does Baljeet believe he is doing when he checks Himani's chats?
qa.a: He believes he only wants the truth and calls it caring, but his long scrolling suggests he feels insecure and suspicious.

qa.q: What turning point is open to Baljeet at this stage?
qa.a: He could notice that demanding her chats is pushing Himani into hiding, stop checking, and talk about his insecurity with her or a school counsellor.

qa.q: How does the checking feel to Himani?
qa.a: To Himani it feels like being watched; she grows nervous, answers carefully and even tells a small, pointless lie that makes her feel sick.

grounding: Shows a jealous teen questioning Himani and demanding to see her chats, which she experiences as being watched until she begins to hide small things.
